_tags: @gotcha("genome/flows/*.md files exist for human reference but are INVISIBLE to agents. Only genome/knowledge/**/*.know files appear in the graph.")
_steps.what: Architecture knowledge lives in .know files under genome/knowledge/. Only .know files are compiled — .md files in genome/flows/ are NOT in the graph. To make knowledge available to agents, it MUST be in a .know file.
python genome.py compile . reads all .know files, extracts flow/concept/entity/test/lesson/decision nodes, resolves references, builds output/graph.json. Run after any .know file change.

GenomeBridge loads graph.json at node startup. contextForTask({taskDescription}) extracts keywords, scores nodes by relevance (primary fields weighted 2x, name 3x, step content 1x), returns top matches formatted as markdown.

buildAIPrompt() calls genomeBridge.contextForTask() with the current inbox messages as task description. Result injected as '## Architecture Knowledge' section. Flows appear first (most actionable), then concepts, entities.
buildBootPrompt() includes genome context in worker's initial prompt. Workers also query /v1/context/project at runtime for on-demand architecture knowledge.

nodes.summary: How architecture knowledge flows from genome documentation to running agents. The genome compiler reads .know files, builds a knowledge graph (output/graph.json), GenomeBridge searches it by keyword relevance, and contextForTask() injects the most relevant nodes into AI prompts. Flows are prioritized over concepts — they describe HOW things work, which is most actionable.

nodes.description: When agents make wrong decisions, check the context pipeline: 1) Is the knowledge in a .know file? (NOT .md) 2) Was the graph recompiled after changes? (python genome.py compile .) 3) Does contextForTask() return the right nodes for the task keywords? (test with node -e in CLI) 4) Does formatNode() render the full content including summary and steps? 5) Is the character budget (6000) not exhausted by irrelevant nodes?

Flow nodes are presented before concepts/entities in contextForTask() output. Rationale: flows describe HOW things work (pipelines, sequences, routing), which is directly actionable. Concepts describe WHAT things are, which is reference info. When an agent asks 'how do I handle a build request?', it needs the ProjectPipeline flow, not the WorkerPool concept.

_steps.what: On node boot (full mode only), PandoNode.startAgentSystem() creates AgentDatabase (SQLite at ~/.pando/agents.db), MessageBus, WorkerPool, OrgManager.
OrgManager.createOrchestrator() creates the council orchestrator — a top-level (level 0) persistent agent identity in AgentDatabase with role 'council'.
Orchestrator(councilOrchId, deps) starts a deterministic tick loop (setInterval). Default: 60s for council. Each tick: read inbox → classify → decide → execute.

_tags: @gotcha("Tier 1 ticks use ZERO AI tokens. Only Tier 2 calls AIBackendRegistry.getBest().")
_steps.what: classify() examines inbox messages. Tier 1 (~80%): deterministic actions (route task results, ack health alerts, check worker status). Tier 2 (~20%): needs AI judgment (new user request, complex health issue, architecture decision).

execute() processes OrchestratorAction[] from either deterministic() or callAI(). 12 action types: spawn_worker, kill_worker, create_task, assign_task, send_message, create_team, dissolve_team, record_lesson, escalate, propose_upgrade, commit_code, deploy, respond_to_user.

_tags: @gotcha("Workers are persistent team members, not disposable. Session IDs saved to SQLite. Resume workers for related tasks to preserve accumulated context. Only rotate when context is exhausted or domain changes.")
@gotcha("Phase 105: Role prompts come from TemplateRegistry (SQLite agent_templates table), not hardcoded DEFAULT_ROLE_PROMPTS. Custom templates can be created via POST /v1/templates.")
_steps.what: WorkerPool.spawn() resolves agent template from TemplateRegistry, then creates or resumes a Claude Code child process. Injects a slim boot prompt (~500 tokens) with identity, task, and context API endpoints. Workers query /v1/context/* on demand for project architecture, lessons, and team state. Workers persist sessions — resumed for related tasks via SessionStrategy. Workers communicate via HTTP: GET /worker/:id/task, POST /worker/:id/report, GET /worker/:id/identity, GET /context/project, GET /context/lessons, GET /context/team, POST /context/discover.
Self-sustaining loop: Orchestrator spawns builder → builder reports completion → Orchestrator spawns QA tester (independent, gets ONLY task + diff) → QA passes → commit + deploy.

_tags: @gotcha("Phase 105: Deployment is agent-driven. No hardcoded onDeploy callback. The devops agent calls the deploy API directly and reports back.")
_steps.what: QA PASS handler (Tier 1 deterministic): commit_code action → spawn devops agent. For projects: devops agent calls POST /v1/projects/:id/deploy and POST /v1/projects/:id/validate-deploy. For council: propose_upgrade → governance → broadcast to all nodes.
Council only: onPropose callback calls governance.createProposal(). In dev mode: auto-approve. Governance decisions route back via MessageBus as 'governance_decision' messages.
reflectOnCompletion() called after task finishes. Extracts lessons from worker reports. High-confidence lessons promote to org_knowledge. Reflection levels: task → project → pattern → organization.

nodes.summary: Orchestrator-based agent system — deterministic tick loop that manages AI workers. Replaces the old Council/AgentManager/BridgeQueue with 5 modules: AgentDatabase, MessageBus, WorkerPool, OrgManager, Orchestrator.

nodes.description: Union type of 13 action types an orchestrator can take per tick: spawn_worker, kill_worker, create_task, assign_task, send_message, create_team, dissolve_team, record_lesson, escalate, propose_upgrade, commit_code, deploy (legacy/noop), respond_to_user, run_scenarios. Returned from deterministic() (Tier 1) or parseAIActions() (Tier 2).

Unified SQLite record for every agent (worker or orchestrator). Fields: id, role, type, scope, parentId, nodeId, status, authority (JSON), fileScope, budget, tickIntervalMs, maxWorkers, rolePrompt, sessionId, templateId, createdAt, updatedAt. Phase 105: templateId links agent instance to its source template.

SQLite-backed persistent message routing. Replaces in-memory BridgeQueue. Enforces communication boundaries: workers → parent only, orchestrators → parent/child/sibling, users → project orchestrator. Messages survive restarts.

Spawn/resume Claude Code worker processes. Manages child_process lifecycle with session persistence. buildBootPrompt() generates a slim ~500-token prompt — workers query /v1/context/* for project architecture, lessons, and discoveries on demand. Workers persist sessions in SQLite — resumed for related tasks, rotated when domain changes. Claude Code is a network resource: discovered via CapabilityProfile (shareCompute: true), not required on every node.

Hierarchy management. createOrchestrator(), dissolve(), getTree(), getOrchestratorForProject(). Authority inheritance via narrowAuthority() — children can never exceed parent's authority. Max depth: 5.

SQLite-backed storage with 8 tables: agent_identity, agent_templates, message_inbox, tick_log, lessons, org_knowledge, directives, reflections. Single file at ~/.pando/agents.db. WAL mode, prepared statements. Phase 105: agent_templates table stores reusable role definitions.

Each orchestrator tick is classified as Tier 1 (deterministic, no AI call) or Tier 2 (needs AI judgment). Examples of Tier 1: route task_result, ack health_alert, check worker timeout. Examples of Tier 2: new user_request, complex escalation, reflection.

nodes.context: Old system had thick Agent class (1,279 lines) with complex state management. New system needed simpler orchestration with persistent workers.
nodes.choice: Persistent workers (session resume, context preservation) + thick orchestrator (deterministic tick loop, all state in SQLite). Claude Code is a discovered network resource, not a node requirement.
nodes.why: 80% of orchestration is deterministic (routing, status checks). Only 20% needs AI. Workers persist sessions via SQLite — resumed for related tasks to preserve accumulated knowledge. Any node with Claude Code contributed (shareCompute: true) can run the council.

nodes.context: BridgeQueue was in-memory. Messages lost on crash. State scattered across JSON files.
nodes.choice: Unified SQLite database (agents.db) for all agent state, messages, lessons, reflections.
nodes.why: Crash recovery. Single source of truth. WAL mode handles concurrent reads. No more scattered state files.

nodes.context: Council needs Claude Code to spawn workers. Not every node has it. Originally assumed council must run on same machine as Claude Code.
nodes.choice: Claude Code is a contributed network resource discovered via CapabilityProfile. Any node contributes via /contribute claude-code (sets shareCompute: true). Council discovers Claude Code nodes via P2P capability registry and routes work there. Council can run on ANY node that has Claude Code — doesn't matter which one.
nodes.why: Same model as MongoDB and API keys — not every node has it, the network discovers who does. Decouples council location from resource location. Multiple nodes can have Claude Code for redundancy.

nodes.context: Workers were killed after each task. Next task on same codebase started from zero. Builder who just learned the storage layer gets deleted, replacement starts blind.
nodes.choice: Workers are persistent team members. Sessions saved to SQLite (sessionId). Resume via claude --continue --resume <sessionId> for related tasks. Rotate only when context exhausted or domain changes completely.
nodes.why: Workers accumulate valuable context — codebase understanding, file locations, gotchas discovered. Throwing this away is wasteful. Lessons in SQLite capture some knowledge, but a resumed session has the full mental model. Team members should persist.

nodes.context: Phase 104. Council orchestrator worked for Pando infra. User app builds (build me X) created project in DB but no live orchestrator was spawned — dead end.
nodes.choice: Same Orchestrator class for both council and projects. Factory method instantiateOrchestrator() determines callbacks based on role. Project orchestrators get onCommit (git in workspace → GitHub push). Deployment is agent-driven: devops worker spawned after QA pass, calls deploy API directly. Workers run in project workspace dir, not Pando repo root.
nodes.why: Council is just Pando's own project manager. No special-casing. Same tick loop, same AI brain, same QA cycle. Only callbacks differ. Deployment through agents enables intelligent decision-making (t1 vs t2, troubleshooting, validation).

nodes.context: Phase 105. Deployment was a hardcoded onDeploy callback — just a fetch() to the deploy endpoint. No intelligence, no troubleshooting, no validation.
nodes.choice: Remove onDeploy callback. After QA passes, orchestrator spawns a devops worker with instructions to call POST /v1/projects/:id/deploy and POST /v1/projects/:id/validate-deploy. Devops agent reads template from TemplateRegistry, can think about the deploy, troubleshoot failures, validate post-deploy.
nodes.why: A callback can't decide 'this needs nginx config changes' or 'the last deploy failed, let me check logs'. An agent can. For simple deploys: agent makes the same HTTP call the callback did. For complex deploys: agent brings intelligence. Templates allow custom devops agents for different deployment environments.

nodes.context: Phase 104. Need project team hierarchy and worker states to be portable and transparent.
nodes.choice: Export team-state.json v2 to project workspace on every commit. Contains: team blueprint (roles + templateIds), cumulative stats, lessons (with relevanceTags), reflections, active directives. Import on clone: lessons with 0.8x confidence decay, reflections, directives.
nodes.why: SQLite is structured and queryable. JSON export travels with the project repo. New node clones and reads it. Users see team structure in GitHub for transparency. v2 format enables full knowledge portability across nodes.

nodes.context: Phase 105. Agent roles were hardcoded as 5 strings in DEFAULT_ROLE_PROMPTS. Adding a new agent type (marketing, news, devops-specialist) required source code changes and redeployment.
nodes.choice: TemplateRegistry class backed by agent_templates SQLite table. Built-in templates seeded on boot (builder, tester, reviewer, researcher, devops). Custom templates created via POST /v1/templates. WorkerPool resolves templates at spawn time. Each agent instance links to its source template via template_id.
nodes.why: Agents are first-class network primitives. Templates are the reusable recipe; instances accumulate their own knowledge per-project. Same devops template → Facebook project learns Facebook patterns, Pando project learns Pando patterns. Schema has publisher_peer_id + version fields ready for future P2P sync and marketplace.

nodes.description: SQLite-backed agent template storage. Replaces hardcoded DEFAULT_ROLE_PROMPTS with data-driven templates. 5 built-in templates seeded on boot. Custom templates via API. Future: P2P sync via GossipSub.

_steps.what: readBoard() collects current state: inbox messages (categorized into workerReports, healthAlerts, userRequests, peerDisconnects, interruptedWorkers), active directives from SQLite, recently failed workers (last 15min), overdue workers, pending tasks, and worker counts.
runHealthMonitoring(board) — always runs (Tier 1). Checks worker health, peer connectivity. Deterministic, no AI call.

_tags: @gotcha("Issue 6 guard: active non-overdue workers + empty inbox = Tier 1. Prevents burning Opus tokens while workers are busy.")
_steps.what: classify(board) returns 1 or 2. Tier 1 when: (a) non-overdue workers active AND inbox empty (let them work), or (b) inbox empty, no directives, not a reflection tick. Tier 2 when: directives exist, reflection tick (every 5th), recently failed/overdue workers, or inbox has messages.

_tags: @gotcha("Tier 1 ticks use ZERO AI tokens. Idle ticks = zero cost.")
_steps.what: Tier 1: deterministic(board) returns actions directly (route results, ack alerts). Tier 2: callAI() sends boot prompt (first tick) or tick update (subsequent ticks) to session-persistent Opus brain. AI returns OrchestratorAction[] via 3-layer JSON parser.

Execute OrchestratorAction[] array. 13 action types: spawn_worker, kill_worker, create_task, assign_task, send_message, create_team, dissolve_team, record_lesson, escalate, propose_upgrade, commit_code, deploy, respond_to_user, run_scenarios.

_tags: @gotcha("markRead guard: if AI call fails, messages stay unread so nothing is lost. Next tick retries.")
_steps.what: messageBus.markRead(allMessageIds) — only if aiError is null. On AI failure, messages are preserved unread for retry on next tick. Agent lastReportAt updated.
db.logTick() records: orchestratorId, tickNumber, tier, boardSnapshot (JSON), actionsExecuted (JSON), aiError if any. Every tick is logged for auditability.

nodes.summary: Single orchestrator tick: classify → readBoard → AI or deterministic → execute → markRead → logTick. Tier 1 = deterministic (no AI, ~2ms). Tier 2 = AI judgment (10-300s).

_steps.what: POST /v1/council/directive receives { content } from operator. Inserts into SQLite directives table with active=1, target_id=councilOrchId, addedBy='operator'.
readBoard().getDirectives() queries SQLite: SELECT * FROM directives WHERE active=1 AND (target_id=? OR target_id IS NULL). Returns as board.directives string array.

_tags: @gotcha("Exception: if non-overdue workers are active AND inbox is empty, stays Tier 1 even with directives — avoids burning tokens while workers are busy.")
_steps.what: classify() checks board.directives.length > 0 — if directives exist, returns Tier 2 (needs AI judgment). Directives always trigger AI thinking.
AI prompt includes '## Directives' section listing all active directive strings. AI decides actions based on directive content.
After orchestrator processes directives, deactivateDirective(id) sets active=0. GET /council/directives shows current active directives.

nodes.summary: Directives are standing orders injected into the orchestrator's AI prompt. They persist in SQLite until explicitly deactivated after processing.

_steps.what: npm run build writes .build-commit file (git commit hash) to packages/node/dist/.build-commit and dist/.build-commit. This stamps which commit the compiled code corresponds to.
Watchdog runs every 5 minutes (setInterval, .unref()). Re-reads .build-commit from disk each cycle (upgrade catch-up may have rebuilt). Compares against git rev-parse HEAD.

_tags: @gotcha("Restart is deferred while workers are active — never kills in-flight work.")
_steps.what: If .build-commit !== HEAD, checks workerPool.getActiveWorkerCount(). If workers > 0, logs 'deferring restart' and waits for next cycle. Active workers are never interrupted.

If .build-commit !== HEAD AND 0 active workers: process.exit(75). Exit code 75 is the RESTART_EXIT_CODE convention. start-node.bat (Windows) and systemd/PM2 (Linux) detect this code and restart the process.
Process manager restarts the node. New process loads the updated compiled code from dist/. Boot health check runs. Agent system rehydrates from SQLite.

nodes.summary: Safe self-restart watchdog detects stale compiled code and exits with code 75 for the process manager (systemd/PM2/start-node.bat) to restart.

_steps.what: PandoNode._start() calls startAgentSystem() in full mode. Creates: AIBackendRegistry (detects Claude + Ollama), AgentDatabase (SQLite), MessageBus, GenomeBridge + GenomeBridgeRegistry, TemplateRegistry, WorkerPool, OrgManager.

_tags: @gotcha("Council identity survives restarts. Only created once — all subsequent boots rehydrate the existing record from SQLite.")
_steps.what: Queries AgentDatabase for existing council orchestrator (role='council', type='orchestrator', status='pending' or 'active'). If found: rehydrate (set status='active'). If not found: OrgManager.createOrchestrator() with role='council', level=0, scope='public', tickInterval=60s, maxWorkers=10.
instantiateOrchestrator(councilOrchId) creates the Orchestrator instance. Factory method determines callbacks based on role: council gets onCommit (git commit + governance proposal), onRestart hooks.
orch.start() begins setInterval tick loop (60s for council). First tick gets full boot prompt with instructions. Subsequent ticks get short board-state update. Session rotates every ~50 ticks.

After council boot, PandoNode also rehydrates persistent project orchestrators from DB (status='active' or 'pending'). Each gets its own instantiateOrchestrator() call with project-specific callbacks.

nodes.summary: How the council orchestrator is created and started during node boot. Survives restarts via SQLite persistence.

_steps.what: Worker calls POST /v1/worker/:id/report with { status:'done'|'error', summary (3000 chars max) }. Auto-report also appends git diff stat. Report stored via messageBus.send() as type='worker_report' to parent orchestrator.
messageBus.send({ type:'worker_report', to: parentOrchId, payload: { status, summary, taskId, auto } }). Message persists in SQLite message_inbox table. Survives restarts.
Next tick: readBoard() categorizes messages. worker_report messages appear in board.workerReports. classify() returns Tier 2 (inbox not empty). AI reads the report in prompt context.

_tags: @gotcha("AI has session memory from previous ticks — it remembers what it asked the worker to do and can evaluate the report in context.")
_steps.what: AI evaluates the worker report. Decisions vary: builder reports done → spawn QA tester. QA reports PASS → commit_code + propose_upgrade. QA reports FAIL → spawn builder with failure details. Genome-updater reports done → commit .know changes.
AI returns OrchestratorAction[] (e.g., spawn_worker with tester role, or commit_code). Actions executed in order. The loop continues: builder → QA → commit → upgrade → next task.

nodes.summary: How worker completion reports flow back to the orchestrator and trigger the next step in the self-sustaining loop.

_steps.what: Clone repo, npm install, npm run build. Or use launcher: start-node.command (Mac) / start-node.bat (Windows).
node packages/node/dist/cli.js --port 4001. Or double-click launcher. Node process starts running.

_tags: @gotcha("On subsequent runs, auto-loads existing identity. Only prompts for password if identity is encrypted.")
_steps.what: TUI silently auto-creates identity on first run (no prompts). Ed25519 keypair generated, encrypted with password (PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM). Stored in ~/.pando/identities/{peerId}.json. Session cached in ~/.pando/session.json.

_tags: @gotcha("Without operator login, node earns no Lux rewards. It operates as relay-only.")
_steps.what: TUI checks for ~/.pando/operator-session.json (auto-login). If found and valid: restores operator state. If not found: node runs as relay-only (no rewards). Operator can /login or /register at any time. On login, node registers itself under user account via POST /auth/me/nodes.
If --bootstrap provided: connect to known peer. If no bootstrap: mDNS discovers local peers. Known-peers from previous sessions are dialed automatically. Auto-connects to EC2 bootstrap by default.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) connect outbound to cloud nodes. Cloud nodes cannot dial back to NAT nodes. This is expected.")
_steps.what: 5s after first peer connects: receives PEER_EXCHANGE with addresses of other nodes in the network. Dials them to form a full mesh. Re-exchange at 30s and 90s catches late-connecting peers. See flow PeerExchange.
LedgerSync requests missing transactions from peers. GossipSub subscribes to all topics. Transactions applied in order until consistent with network state.
First-time node registration: receives genesis Lux. Early multiplier: accounts 1-100 get 5x, 101-1000 get 3x, 1001-10000 get 2x.
API server listening on --api-port (default 4000). P2P listening on --port. Optional: start gateway, scheduler (--scheduler), monitor (--monitor). Full node operational.

nodes.summary: How a new node joins the Pando network. Install, start, create identity, optionally login as operator, connect to peers, sync ledger, receive genesis allocation, and become fully operational.

_tags: @gotcha("identify protocol takes 1-3s to complete. updateKnownPeer is delayed 3s to ensure peerStore has announce addresses before persisting.")
_steps.what: New peer connects via bootstrap or known-peers dial. libp2p identify protocol runs automatically, exchanging listen/announce addresses. Announce addresses (public IPs) are stored in the peerStore.

_tags: @gotcha("EC2 nodes in the same VPC connect via internal IPs (172.31.x.x). Without peerStore addresses, known-peers would only store internal IPs that external nodes cannot dial.")
_steps.what: updateKnownPeer() saves both connection addresses AND peerStore announce addresses to ~/.pando/known-peers.json. This ensures public IPs are persisted even when the actual TCP connection uses internal/VPC IPs.

5s after connect: node sends PEER_EXCHANGE message to the new peer. Payload contains all connected peers' addresses (connection addrs + known-peers + peerStore announce addrs). Filtered to exclude the recipient's own address.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) cannot be dialed from cloud nodes. They connect outbound. This is expected — peer exchange helps them discover cloud nodes, not the other way around.")
_steps.what: Receiving node parses peer list, skips already-connected peers, tries to dial each unknown peer using the shared addresses. Tries all addresses for each peer until one works.
Delayed re-exchange at 30s and 90s after boot broadcasts the full peer list to all connected peers. This catches peers that connected after the initial 5s exchange window.

Combined with known-peers persistence (7-day TTL, 50-peer cap), peer exchange ensures full mesh formation within ~90s of boot. On restart, known-peers are dialed immediately, providing instant reconnection.

nodes.summary: Peer exchange protocol — nodes share peer addresses on connect so new nodes can form a full mesh without a central hub. Replaces the need for a relay/bootstrap hub.

_steps.what: Every 5 minutes, select a random connected peer.

_tags: @gotcha("With fewer than 6 peers, GossipSub mesh may be too thin for reliable message propagation. This timer ensures governance decisions reach all nodes regardless.")
_steps.what: Request governance catch-up from the selected peer. Peer sends all proposals/votes/decisions the requesting node hasn't seen.
Apply received governance state. This catches upgrade proposals, votes, and decisions that were missed via GossipSub.

nodes.summary: Periodic governance re-sync — every 5 minutes, nodes request governance state from a random peer. Safety net for thin GossipSub meshes where votes/decisions may not propagate.

_steps.what: User sends POST /v1/chat/message with 'build me a landing page'. No projectId.
doormanClassify() uses OpenAI gpt-4o-mini to determine intent. Returns 'build' with tier (1=static, 2=server) and description.
projectStore.createProject() creates record in MongoDB (via P2P proxy for untrusted nodes). Assigns MongoDB + GitHub resources via preflight.

ensureProjectWorkspace(projectId) creates ~/.pando/projects/<projectId>/, runs git init. If project has githubRepo, clones it first. Workers query /v1/context/project for architecture context on demand — no CLAUDE.md needed.

_tags: @gotcha("Same Orchestrator class as council. Only callbacks differ.")
_steps.what: ensureProjectOrchestrator(projectId) calls OrgManager.getOrchestratorForProject() for DB record, then instantiateOrchestrator() for live instance. Factory wires project-scoped callbacks: onCommit (git in workspace → GitHub push), onDeploy (S3/PM2+nginx).
Orchestrator.start() begins 30s tick loop. First tick reads user_request from MessageBus inbox. Tier 2 → calls AI to plan approach.

_tags: @gotcha("Worker cwd = config.workspaceDir (project workspace). Workers write files HERE, not in Pando root.")
_steps.what: AI brain returns spawn_worker action with role='builder'. WorkerPool.spawn() creates Claude Code process in project workspace dir (not Pando repo root).

Builder receives slim boot prompt with task + context API endpoints. Queries /v1/context/project for architecture and discoveries, writes code, runs build, posts new discoveries via /v1/context/discover, reports 'done' via POST /v1/worker/:id/report.
Deterministic Tier 1: builder done → spawn tester worker. Tester gets ONLY task description + code diff. Independent verification.
Tester runs in same project workspace. Checks code quality, tests functionality, reports PASS or FAIL.
Deterministic Tier 1: QA PASS → commit_code action. onCommit callback: exportTeamState() → git add -A → git commit in workspace → POST /projects/:id/github/push.
After commit, orchestrator may trigger deploy action. onDeploy callback: POST /v1/projects/:id/deploy → P2P discovery → compute peer → S3 (tier 1) or PM2+nginx (tier 2).
respond_to_user action sends live URL via MessageBus → SSE to gateway.

nodes.summary: Phase 104: End-to-end flow for user app creation. Chat message → doorman classifies 'build' → project created → workspace initialized → project orchestrator instantiated → builder spawns → QA verifies → commit to workspace → push to GitHub → deploy to S3/nginx.

nodes.description: Phase 104: Each user project gets a local directory at ~/.pando/projects/<projectId>/. Contains the project's git repo, team-state.json, and all source code. Workers run with cwd set to this directory. Context comes from /v1/context/project (genome if compiled, or auto-generated from package.json + file tree). On commit, pushed to GitHub as pando-lux/app-<id>-<name>.

Phase 104: JSON file (team-state.json) exported to project workspace on every commit. Contains agent list (id, role, status, sessionId, budgetSpent), lessons. Committed to git → pushed to GitHub → cloned by new nodes for resume. Enables transparency (users see team in GitHub) and continuity (new orchestrator reads previous state).

Phase 104: PandoNode.instantiateOrchestrator(orchId) is the unified factory for ALL orchestrators. Reads DB record, determines callbacks based on role (council → git in Pando repo + governance, project → git in workspace + GitHub push + deploy). Stores live instances in Map<string, Orchestrator>. Used by council startup, project creation, and rehydration on restart.

_tags: @gotcha("pushToArray fails SILENTLY via P2P proxy — no error, no log, no thrown exception. The only symptom is the array staying empty while the document's scalar counters increment. Always test on an untrusted (non-direct-MongoDB) node.")

@gotcha("The split-brain manifests as: thread.messageCount grows (putRecord succeeds), but thread.messages[] is always [] (pushToArray silently discarded). Looks like an async race condition — it is not. The async fix (d719e757) was correct but insufficient.")
nodes.description: ARCHITECTURAL GOTCHA (confirmed 2026-02-28, commit 7ce9a282): storageBackend.pushToArray() ($push operator) FAILS SILENTLY when routed through the P2P storage proxy. The proxy returns HTTP 200 success but the write never reaches the underlying MongoDB collection. This causes array fields to stay empty while scalar fields (e.g. messageCount) increment correctly — a split-brain symptom. ONLY safe to use pushToArray on trusted nodes with a direct PANDO_STORAGE_URL connection. For all other paths, use the read-modify-write pattern: getRecord() → mutate array in memory → putRecord() with $set.

nodes.context: thread-store.ts addMessage() used storageBackend.pushToArray($push) to append messages. On nodes without PANDO_STORAGE_URL (P2P proxy path), pushToArray returned success but the $push never reached MongoDB. getMessagesAsync() returned [] despite messageCount incrementing. Root cause surfaced in commit 7ce9a282 after ruling out async race conditions (d719e757) and schema mismatches.
nodes.choice: Replace ALL pushToArray calls in the P2P-proxied code path with a read-modify-write pattern: (1) getRecord() to fetch the full document, (2) append to the target array in memory (document.field = [...(document.field || []), newItem]), (3) putRecord() with $set to write the full document back. This is the reliable pattern for P2P proxy nodes.
nodes.why: The P2P storage proxy translates putRecord($set) correctly but does not support the MongoDB $push operator. pushToArray is only safe with a direct MongoDB connection (PANDO_STORAGE_URL set on trusted nodes). Using read-modify-write with $set works through the proxy because it is a simple document replacement, not an operator. Any future array append operations in P2P-proxied collections must follow this pattern.

_tags: @gotcha("This is a proxy capability gap, not a MongoDB limitation. Direct-connection nodes (EC2-1, EC2-2 with PANDO_STORAGE_URL set) work fine with pushToArray. The bug only surfaces on user nodes or untrusted relays routing through the P2P proxy.")
nodes.description: The P2P storage proxy (request-reply.ts routing to a trusted peer's StorageBackend) supports a subset of MongoDB operations. Confirmed WORKING via proxy: putRecord($set, upsert), getRecord, deleteRecord, listRecords. Confirmed BROKEN via proxy: pushToArray($push) — silently discarded. Any code calling pushToArray must assume it will fail on non-trusted-compute nodes. If P2P array writes are needed in the future, the proxy handler must be extended to support $push translation.

_tags: @gotcha("Use --data-dir /tmp/pando-test to avoid polluting default ~/.pando")
nodes.description: Node starts, creates Ed25519 identity, persists across restarts. Same peerId on restart.
steps: Verify identity file exists in data-dir/identities/
nodes.expected: peerId identical across restarts. Identity file persisted on disk.

_tags: @gotcha("TUI password prompt requires human interaction — not automatable")
nodes.description: Encrypted identity with password. Correct password restores same peerId. Wrong password fails cleanly.

_tags: @gotcha("Session-aware: tries loadSession() first for encrypted identities. If session.json exists, the node starts with that identity without prompting for password.")
@gotcha("Port pre-check: if API port is occupied, CLI attempts to shut down the existing instance via POST /admin/shutdown before failing.")
@gotcha("RESTART_EXIT_CODE = 75 — PM2/systemd/start-node.bat restarts the process when it exits with this code.")
@gotcha("MSYS2 path normalization: /c/Users/... is converted to C:\\Users\\... on Windows because path.join mishandles MSYS2 paths.")
@why("DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAPS contains 3 nodes (LS-1, EC2-1, EC2-2) for mesh connectivity — ensures new nodes connect to at least 2 bootstrap peers.")
@why("Public IP auto-detection uses AWS IMDS v1 (http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/public-ipv4) with 2s timeout — works on EC2 and Lightsail, silently skips elsewhere.")
nodes.description: Non-interactive CLI entry point: parses flags, initializes PandoNode with MongoDB/storage backend, sets up file logging, crash guard, port pre-check, post-deploy health checks, and heartbeat reporting.

nodes.what: Node failed to start because previous instance still held the API port
nodes.why: PM2 restart or crash left the old process running, and Fastify's listen() fails immediately on EADDRINUSE
nodes.fix: Added port pre-check that attempts graceful shutdown of existing instance via /admin/shutdown API, waits up to 15s for port release

_tags: @gotcha("PandoNode is a GOD OBJECT with 50+ private fields — each subsystem is nullable and initialized conditionally during start(). Always null-check before use.")
@gotcha("detectClaudeCode() has a 3-second timeout — on slow systems (Windows especially) this can delay startup.")
@gotcha("Daily emission cap (500 Lux) is tracked in-memory (dailyEmissions) and reset by date string comparison — restarting the node resets the counter.")

@gotcha("Peer exchange runs at 5s after each peer connect, plus 30s and 90s after boot. It shares addresses from getConnectedPeerAddresses() which includes peerStore announce addresses for NAT/VPC traversal.")
@gotcha("Governance re-sync runs every 5 min to catch missed votes/decisions in thin GossipSub meshes (<6 peers).")
@why("Subsystems are initialized in layered order: kernel (network, ledger, sync) -> core (agents, storage) -> platform (scheduler, resources). This matches the import boundary rule.")
nodes.description: Main PandoNode class that wires together all subsystems (kernel, core, platform layers), manages startup/shutdown lifecycle, and exposes getters for every subsystem.

_tags: @gotcha("GossipSub topic subscriptions are deduplicated — subscribing twice to the same topic is a no-op. All topic listeners are cleaned up in stop() to prevent leaks on restart.")
@gotcha("Known peers are persisted to ~/.pando/known-peers.json with 7-day TTL and 50-peer cap. On startup, known peers are re-dialed automatically.")
@gotcha("Peer exchange includes peerStore announce addresses (public IPs from identify protocol), not just connection addresses. This is critical for NAT/VPC traversal.")
@gotcha("Agent message payload limit is 256KB (increased from 8KB) to support P2P storage proxy responses containing large project/thread data.")
@why("announce addresses are configured via PUBLIC_IP env var on cloud nodes — required because 0.0.0.0 bind address is not externally reachable behind NAT/VPC.")
@why("updateKnownPeer is delayed 3s after connect to allow the identify protocol to populate peerStore with announce addresses.")
nodes.description: Core P2P networking layer built on libp2p with TCP+Noise encryption, Yamux muxing, mDNS/bootstrap discovery, GossipSub pub/sub, and circuit relay support.

nodes.why: Node.js may resolve localhost to ::1 (IPv6) which libp2p/Fastify may not bind
nodes.fix: Always use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost for local connections

nodes.what: Cross-node auth failed because ledger stored 'remote-peer' as public key
nodes.why: Remote nodes registered with placeholder public key, making signature verification impossible
nodes.fix: Extract public key from peerId string via peerIdFromString().publicKey — no ledger lookup needed

nodes.what: Peer exchange shared internal VPC IPs (172.31.x.x) that external nodes could not dial
nodes.why: EC2 nodes in the same VPC connect via internal IPs. connection.remoteAddr returns the internal IP, not the public announce address.
nodes.fix: getConnectedPeerAddresses() and updateKnownPeer() now also query libp2p peerStore for announce addresses (public IPs from identify protocol). AWS IMDS auto-detects public IP on cloud nodes.

nodes.rule: Each GossipSub topic must only be subscribed once per PandoNetwork instance — subscribedTopics Set enforces this

_tags: @gotcha("Entries are FIFO — oldest entries are dropped when max is reached. Flow names should be consistent across runs for briefings to be useful.")
@why("QA agents with zero context about changes need SOME context about historically-broken areas. QA Memory provides that without revealing what was changed.")
nodes.description: Phase 101d: Persistent store of past QA results. Learns from test failures to feed historical context into adversarial QA agents. Stored at {dataDir}/council/qa-memory.json (max 500 entries).

_tags: @gotcha("MESSAGE_VERSION = 1 — must be incremented when envelope format changes, or P2P messages will be silently dropped by peers on different versions.")
@gotcha("OperationalMode 1/2/3 maps to local-only / P2P / full (P2P + internet infra). Mode 1 must always be available offline.")
@gotcha("LUX_HARD_CAP = 10,000,000,000 — this constant is the single source of truth for the Lux supply ceiling, checked in TransactionStore.emit().")
@gotcha("MessageType.PEER_EXCHANGE is handled in PandoNode (index.ts), not PandoNetwork — it's an application-level protocol, not a kernel primitive.")
@why("NodeHealth tracks per-layer boot status (kernel/core/platform) so the node can degrade gracefully instead of crashing entirely.")
nodes.description: All shared types, interfaces, enums, and constants used across every Pando package — identity, messages, transactions, governance, agents, capabilities, and economics.

nodes.rule: LUX_HARD_CAP (10 billion) must never be changed without Tier 1 governance vote (90% quorum + 30-day migration)
